facts: Alex L. Zhang, Tim Kraska, and Omar Khattab authored the paper 'Recursive Language Models' on arXiv (arXiv:2512.24601) on December 31, 2025.
The paper introduces Recursive Language Models (RLMs), a general inference paradigm that approaches long prompt processing through inference-time scaling.
RLMs treat long prompts as part of an external environment and allow the LLM to programmatically examine, decompose, and recursively call itself over snippets.
RLMs successfully process inputs up to two orders of magnitude beyond model context windows while maintaining comparable cost.
Across four diverse long-context tasks on GPT-5, RLMs achieved median improvements of 26% against compaction, 130% against CodeAct with sub-calls, and 13% against Claude Code.
The authors post-trained RLM-Qwen3-8B, which improved over Qwen3-8B by 28.3% on average and approached vanilla GPT-5 quality on three long-context tasks.
The official implementation code is available at https://github.com/alexzhang13/rlm.
